summary: Diagnose wrong captions (not the real speech/rhythm) and reference-video fidelity + smooth motion; design fixes

findings.summary: Captions that have nothing to do with the speech come from one main source. In the demo/local path, whenever Whisper does not return segments, lib/ai/demo.ts demoCaptions() makes "example captions" out of the words of the user's BRIEF (or a fixed demo sentence). It spreads them evenly at about 0.42 s per word over the stretches that have sound. I reproduced this in a real browser (Pixel 7 emulation, c3c7dac build, a video with real pt-BR speech): with Whisper on, the captions were the real speech, 26.9% WER with whisper-tiny, and the caption gaps matched the real pauses. In every other case the captions were the brief repeated ("Vídeo dinâmico para Reels da minha confeitaria…", ~96% WER, no gaps during pauses). That happened with CC off, "Pular legendas", a failed model download, a music-only clip ("Não encontrei fala" and then fake captions anyway), and re-running "Editar com IA" after Undo, where the triedTranscription cache silently skips Whisper. The same text gets in with the badge showing "Claude": chat "coloque legenda" plus a skip, or CC off, sends generateCaptions to demoCaptions. Separately, the server validator accepts set_captions/update_caption text that Claude invents when there is no transcript, and the prompt never forbids it. Demo captions are also sent to Claude as if they were the transcript, with word ids. Given the stuck "Demo" badge (every first edit ran the demo branch), the most likely cause on Bruno's phone is that Whisper produced nothing and the planner filled the captions with the brief's words, which fits both complaints: wrong text and no speech rhythm. The exact trigger (skip, download failure, undo+rerun) needs his chat log. A second, smaller cause is whisper-tiny on mobile: 26.9% WER against 9.6% for whisper-base on the same audio.

rootCauses.claim: In demo mode the first edit inserts 'example captions' made from the BRIEF's words whenever the project has no captions. That covers Whisper skipped, failed, stalled, disabled, or finding no speech. The words are spread evenly over the stretches with sound, so neither the text nor the rhythm comes from the speech.
rootCauses.evidence: lib/ai/demo.ts:514-518 demoWordPool (brief words, or the fixed sentence 'Este é um exemplo de legenda automática…' when the brief has fewer than 4 words); demo.ts:521-539 demoCaptions (n = (end-start)/0.42 words, distributeWords = uniform split weighted by word length); demo.ts:593-606 planFirstEdit step 1 runs when intent.captions && !p.captions.segments.length; pipeline.ts:302-308 demo branch calls planFirstEdit after whisperCaptions returned null or []. Playwright (Pixel 7, demo, 18.7 s Piper pt-BR video, 52-word reference): scenarios off, skip and fail each produced 7 captions = brief text repeated, WER 96.2%, continuous 0–16.38 s with no gaps; real pauses on the timeline are about 4.10–4.62, 8.50–9.06 and 12.21–12.80 s.

rootCauses.claim: Even when Whisper works and finds no speech (returns []), the demo first edit still adds fake captions. The chat log contradicts itself: 'Não encontrei fala para legendar' followed by fake captions.
rootCauses.evidence: pipeline.ts:262-265: segs=[] only logs 'Não encontrei fala'; then planFirstEdit (demo.ts:597) sees no captions and calls demoCaptions. Measured with a 12 s music-only clip: Whisper ran, the chat logged 'Não encontrei fala para legendar', and 5 captions of brief text were applied over 0–12 s.

rootCauses.claim: The triedTranscription cache makes any second first edit skip Whisper silently (after Undo / 'Voltar para antes desta edição' / running 'Editar com IA' again). In demo mode that gives brief-text captions; in Claude mode Claude gets captions: [].
rootCauses.evidence: pipeline.ts:177 module-level Set; :181 filters already-tried media; :201 adds the asset before transcribing (success, empty or failure); only generateCaptions clears it (:360). runFirstEdit and ensureWords never retry. Measured (RERUN): 1st run gave 9 real captions ('Hoje vamos mostrar como fazer um bolo'…); Undo + run again gave 7 brief captions with no Whisper attempt, and the reply wrongly says 'a transcrição foi pulada'. Mock-Claude RERUN: 1st /api/ai/edit body had 9 captions, the 2nd had 0.

rootCauses.claim: The fake-caption fallback also runs in Claude mode. generateCaptions (chat 'coloque legenda…', CC button 'Gerar legendas', 'Legendas auto') falls back to demoCaptions whenever Whisper returns null without a warning, i.e. user skipped/aborted or the CC preference is off. It throws only on an actual failure.
rootCauses.evidence: pipeline.ts:362-373 (`if (status.configured && warnings.length) throw` else demoCaptions(…, project.brief)); :182 opts.whisper===false returns null with no warning; chatStore.ts:101-104,156 ('ep_ai_whisper'='off' preference). Measured with mocked status configured:true (badge 'Claude'): chat 'coloque legenda no vídeo' + 'Pular legendas' gave 7 brief captions, reply 'Coloquei 7 legendas de exemplo nos trechos de fala (sem transcrição desta vez)'. Same result with CC off, without even asking.

rootCauses.claim: Claude can write caption text that is not the speech. validate.ts accepts set_captions with any text (word timings are synthesized evenly and given ids), and update_caption rewrites text with uniform timings. The first-edit task tells Claude to 'Aplique legendas' even when captions.count = 0, and the prompt has no rule against inventing caption text. Whether Claude actually does this in production is a hypothesis (no API key here).
rootCauses.evidence: validate.ts:505-510 (set_captions → sanitizeSegments → sanitizeTranscript/assignWordIds, no transcript check), :511-531 (update_caption text → uniform words); sanitize.ts:331 distributeWords when words are missing; app/api/ai/edit/route.ts:91 'Aplique legendas no estilo certo…'; prompts/edit-system.md:62-63 (only 'só se pedirem legendas novas/reescritas'). vite-node check: sanitizeOps([{op:'set_captions',segments:[{text:'Pão quentinho toda manhã'},{text:'Siga para mais!'}]}]) on a project with 0 captions gives 1 op accepted, 0 dropped, ids w00001…w00007 at uniform times.

rootCauses.claim: Once fake captions exist they stick, and they poison later AI edits. They are saved in IndexedDB, they block every automatic re-transcription (first edit and chat need captions to be empty), and they are sent to Claude as THE transcript with word ids, so remove_words/hooks/highlights act on invented words.
rootCauses.evidence: lib/persist/index.ts:27-31 saves project incl. captions; pipeline.ts:259 and :548 require !captions.segments.length; summary.ts:56-62 sends segments with '[wNNNNN t0-t1] word'; vite-node check printed the demo captions as Claude would see them: '[w00001 0.00-0.37] Vídeo [w00002 0.37-0.95] dinâmico…'.

rootCauses.claim: MOST LIKELY scenario on Bruno's Android: before c3c7dac, one failed /api/ai/status check was cached, so the whole session stayed in demo and runFirstEdit ran the demo branch. Whisper then returned nothing. Possible triggers: 'Pular legendas' on a 'weak' device, the 41–63 MB model download failing or stalling on the same flaky mobile connection that broke the status check, CC off, no speech detected, or (silently) a second run after Undo. planFirstEdit then filled the captions with his brief's words spread evenly. This matches both complaints (unrelated text and not following the speaker's rhythm). A working Whisper, even tiny, gives recognisable text with gaps that match the pauses. The exact trigger cannot be pinned down without his chat log: 'Transcrição pulada' / 'A transcrição falhou neste navegador (…)' / 'Não encontrei fala' / no line at all for a re-run.
rootCauses.evidence: client.ts:93-102 (c3c7dac diff: the old getStatus cached `.catch(()=>({configured:false}))` for the whole session); pipeline.ts:278 vs 302 branch on status.configured; frames.ts:24 weak = deviceMemory<=3 || (cores<=4 && mobile), and the Pixel 7 emulation reported cores=4, so the 'Transcrever (~41 MB) / Pular legendas' question appeared; whisper.ts:40-48 mobile uses tiny (63 MB WebGPU f16 / 41 MB WASM q8). Measured caption timing: Whisper caption gaps 4.36–4.86, 8.86–9.28 and 12.36–12.94 are within about 0.25 s of the real pauses; demo captions have no gaps at all.

rootCauses.claim: Secondary: when Whisper does run on a phone, whisper-tiny (q8) noticeably garbles Portuguese. Some caption words are wrong even though the timing is right.
rootCauses.evidence: Same audio: mobile tiny q8 WASM WER 26.9% ('Primeiro, você para 3 ovos, uma x' / '-creditação cargador e 2 x -cres'); speech + loud music (music about 4 dB under the voice) 25.0%; desktop whisper-base q8 9.6% ('Primeiro, se parê 3 ovos, uma xícara de açúcar e 2 xícaras de farinha.'). This is clean TTS; real phone audio is expected to be worse (hypothesis). The WebGPU fp16/q4f16 path used on many Androids could not be tested (no adapter in headless Chromium).

rootCauses.claim: Minor non-speech text paths: (a) the demo first edit copies the reference video's on-screen text (Claude analysis textOverlays.examples[0]) as a big uppercase title at 0–2.5 s, which can look like a caption; (b) chatIntent can still create demoCaptions in edge cases (demo + 'traduz … e coloca legenda': the translate branch returns null in demo, so demoChat runs with silences); (c) the demo reply says 'a transcrição foi pulada' even when it failed or was never tried.
rootCauses.evidence: demo.ts:627 `hook = intent.hook ?? style?.textOverlays?.examples?.[0]`; prompts/analyze-reference.md:32 'até 8 textos que aparecem na tela'; pipeline.ts:579 (`if (!status.configured) return null`) then demo.ts:818-825; demo.ts:693 reply text; fail scenario chat: 'A transcrição falhou neste navegador (…transformers.min.js)' followed by '…(a transcrição foi pulada)'.

proposals.title: Remove every fake-caption generator (captions only from a real transcription)
proposals.details: Delete demoCaptions/demoWordPool use in: demo.ts planFirstEdit step 1 (lines 593-606; keep only set_caption_style so the style applies when real captions arrive), pipeline.ts generateCaptions fallback (364-373) and demo.ts chatIntent (820-825). When whisperCaptions returns null or [], apply no set_captions. Return a typed reason instead: {status:'skipped'|'disabled'|'failed'|'no_speech', error?}. Keep `exampleCaptions` logic out. Add vitest: runFirstEdit/generateCaptions/chatEdit with transcribeMedia mocked to throw, abort, or return [] must emit no set_captions op and the reply must say why.

proposals.title: Replace triedTranscription with a per-asset transcript cache
proposals.details: pipeline.ts:177-217: change the Set into Map<`${asset.id}|${asset.url}`, CaptionSegment[] (media time)> that stores only successful results. runFirstEdit/ensureWords reuse the cached transcript instantly after Undo / re-run (map with captionsMediaToTimeline against the current project) and retry on failure. Keep a short in-memory 'failed in this command' guard only to avoid loops within one run. Optionally persist the media-time transcript on MediaAsset (additive field, e.g. asset.transcript?) so a reload doesn't need to re-transcribe.

proposals.title: Honest UX when transcription is unavailable
proposals.details: In the run log and reply, say exactly what happened: 'Legendas não colocadas: transcrição pulada', 'falhou (motivo)', 'CC desligado' or 'não encontrei fala'. Add buttons in ChatPanel/AiPopup: 'Tentar transcrever de novo' (calls generateCaptions), 'Ligar CC' when the preference is off, and 'Escrever legendas manualmente' (opens Legendas tab). On mobile with flaky network, offer 'Transcrever depois (no Wi‑Fi)'. Fix demo.ts:693 so the reply no longer claims 'a transcrição foi pulada' when it failed.

proposals.title: Server-side guard: Claude never authors caption text
proposals.details: validate.ts sanitizeOp: drop `set_captions` coming from Claude (route.ts mode first/chat/comments) unless every word text matches the existing transcript words in order, i.e. it only re-segments or retimes. Drop update_caption.patch.text unless mode==='chat' and the request targets that caption (context.segmentId) or explicitly asks to fix/correct a word. When a text fix is allowed, keep the original word timings by token alignment instead of redistributing evenly (validate.ts:525-527). Translation stays on its own route (/api/ai/translate) and is labelled as a translation.

proposals.title: Prompt + summary: tell Claude when there is no transcript
proposals.details: prompts/edit-system.md: add rule 'Legendas = só a fala transcrita. Se captions.count = 0 não crie legendas nem use brief/gancho/textos do modelo como legenda; diga no reply que a transcrição não está disponível. Nunca reescreva texto de legenda sem pedido explícito.' app/api/ai/edit/route.ts:91: make 'Aplique legendas' conditional on captions existing. summary.ts: add captions.transcribed:boolean / source so Claude knows whether the words are real.

proposals.title: Caption provenance in the contract + detect legacy fake captions
proposals.details: Additive lib/types.ts: Captions.source?: 'transcription' | 'manual' | 'translation' plus model label (test in ops.test.ts). The pipeline sets it, the panel shows a chip ('Transcrição automática · Whisper base'). For projects already saved in IndexedDB with demo captions (no source): when segment words equal the demoWordPool(project.brief) sequence or the fixed demo sentence, flag them as 'legendas de exemplo antigas' and offer 'Refazer pela fala'. Also let chat 'coloque legenda' re-transcribe when existing captions are not source==='transcription'.

proposals.title: Better Whisper model on capable phones
proposals.details: whisper.ts chooseWhisper: use whisper-base for mobile when not weak (WebGPU f16 about 110 MB, WASM q8 about 77 MB) and keep tiny only for weak devices or as the user's 'Rápido' choice. Measured on the same audio: tiny 26.9% WER vs base 9.6%. Add a sanity check on output (repeated tokens, words not in the dictionary, chars/sec out of range) and fall back from WebGPU q4f16 to WASM q8 when the output looks degenerate (WebGPU garbage output is a hypothesis to verify on a real Android). Reconsider frames.ts:24 weak rule (cores<=4) so the 'Pular legendas' question is not triggered unnecessarily.

proposals.title: Do not copy the reference video's on-screen text into the user's video
proposals.details: demo.ts:627: stop using style.textOverlays.examples[0] as the hook text; use the reference only for typography/position. In prompts/edit-system.md 'Aplicando o estilo', state that textOverlays.examples are style samples and must not be copied verbatim.

proposals.title: Regression E2E with real speech
proposals.details: Add to e2e a Piper pt_BR fixture (my scratch: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/aa48c5f3-da7a-51ea-a4c5-276a3a3dd31a/scratchpad/diag/captions-src/fala.mp4 + speech.txt, reproducible via piper-tts + rhasspy pt_BR-faber-medium). Assert on Pixel 7 + desktop: (1) captions WER < 35% vs speech.txt and caption gaps within 0.4 s of the real pauses; (2) with CC off / 'Pular legendas' / HF blocked / music-only / undo+rerun, zero captions are created and the brief's words never appear in captions.

findings.report:
## Scope
Every code path that can put text into `project.captions` that is not the person's real speech. Code is at HEAD c3c7dac; `lib/ai`, `prompts` and `app/api/ai` have not changed since then (checked with `git diff c3c7dac HEAD`). I edited no repository files. All experiment files are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/aa48c5f3-da7a-51ea-a4c5-276a3a3dd31a/scratchpad/diag/captions-src/`.

## 1. Paths that create caption segments
| # | Path | Where the text comes from | When it fires |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `runFirstEdit` demo → `planFirstEdit` step 1 (demo.ts:593-606) | **brief words** via `demoWordPool` (demo.ts:514-518), or the fixed sentence "Este é um exemplo de legenda automática no modo demonstração do EditorPro" when the brief has fewer than 4 words. Timing is even, about 0.42 s/word, inside "sound" ranges (demo.ts:521-539). | Demo mode, captions empty, brief has no "sem legenda", and Whisper returned null **or []**. Triggers: CC off (`ep_ai_whisper=off`), "Pular legendas", Pular button (abort), failure or 90 s stall, no speech, or media already in `triedTranscription` (re-run). |
| B | `generateCaptions` fallback (pipeline.ts:362-373) | brief words (`project.brief`) | **Both modes** when Whisper returned null without a warning (skip, abort, CC off, nothing to transcribe). In Claude mode it throws only on a real failure (:366). Reached from chat "coloque legenda…" (localFeature :548-553), the CC button "Gerar legendas" and mobile "Legendas auto". |
| C | `chatIntent` (demo.ts:818-825) | brief words | Demo chat when localFeature doesn't catch the request, e.g. "traduz … e coloca legenda" (translate branch returns null in demo, :579). |
| D | Claude `set_captions` (validate.ts:505-510) | anything Claude writes; words synthesized evenly with ids | Accepted with no transcript check. First-edit task says "Aplique legendas no estilo certo" (route.ts:91) even with 0 captions; the prompt (edit-system.md:62-63) doesn't forbid inventing. *Whether Claude actually does it in production: hypothesis (no key here).* |
| E | Claude `update_caption.text` (validate.ts:511-531) | Claude rewrite; words redistributed evenly | Any mode. |
| F | Translation (pipeline.ts:577-592) | Claude translation, `distributeWords` timings | Explicit request: intended, but the speech rhythm is lost. |
| G | Whisper (whisper.ts → words.ts → timemap.ts) | real speech, word timestamps | Real. Quality depends on the model: mobile uses **tiny** (whisper.ts:40-48). |
| H | Manual "Nova legenda" (CaptionsTab.tsx:43-47) | user | Intended. |
| I (text clip, not a caption) | demo hook = `style.textOverlays.examples[0]` (demo.ts:627) | reference video's on-screen text | Demo first edit with a Claude-analyzed reference. |

**Stickiness:** fake captions are saved to IndexedDB (persist/index.ts:27-31). They block every automatic re-transcription (pipeline.ts:259 and :548 require empty captions). They are given word ids by `sanitizeSegments` (validate.ts:331-335) and sent to Claude as the transcript (summary.ts:56-62). vite-node output: `[w00001 0.00-0.37] Vídeo [w00002 0.37-0.95] dinâmico…`. Claude would then cut, highlight or build hooks from invented words.

**Validator check (vite-node):** an invented `set_captions` on a project with 0 captions gives `accepted: 1, dropped: 0`, with words `w00001@0-0.429 … w00007@4.846-6`.

## 2. Browser simulation
Setup: own server on :3102, `/dev/chat` harness, Playwright with Pixel 7 emulation (UA Android, `hardwareConcurrency=4`, so `deviceProfile().weak=true` and the "Transcrever (~41 MB) / Pular legendas" question appears), demo mode (no key). Material: an 18.7 s 540×960 video with Piper pt_BR speech (`pt_BR-faber-medium`, 4 sentences, 52 words, 1 s lead-in).

Brief: "Vídeo dinâmico para Reels da minha confeitaria, com legenda amarela e cores quentes".

Real pauses (silencedetect, media time): 5.20–5.72, 9.60–10.16, 13.31–13.90. After the first edit cuts 1.1 s at the start, these sit at about 4.10–4.62, 8.50–9.06, 12.21–12.80 on the timeline.

| Scenario | Who produced the text | Captions | WER vs speech | Rhythm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whisper on (tiny q8, WASM, 41 MB download, 17.3 s total) | Whisper | 9: "Hoje vamos mostrar como fazer um bolo" / "Primeiro, você para 3 ovos, uma x" / "-creditação cargador e 2 x -cres" / … | 26.9% | gaps at 4.36–4.86, 8.86–9.28, 12.36–12.94: aligned (±0.25 s) |
| Speech + loud music (music about 4 dB under the voice) | Whisper tiny | 8 | 25.0% | aligned |
| Desktop (whisper-base q8, 77 MB) | Whisper base | 8: "Primeiro, se parê 3 ovos, uma xícara de açúcar e 2 xícaras de farinha." | **9.6%** | aligned |
| CC off (`ep_ai_whisper=off`) | demoCaptions (brief) | 7: "Vídeo dinâmico para Reels da minha" / "confeitaria, com legenda amarela e cores" / "quentes Vídeo dinâmico…" | 96% | continuous 0–16.38, no gaps |
| "Pular legendas" | demoCaptions (brief) | same 7 | 96.2% | none |
| Model download blocked (HF/jsDelivr aborted) | demoCaptions (brief) | same 7; reply says "a transcrição foi pulada" | 96.2% | none |
| Music only, no speech (12 s) | Whisper ran ("Não encontrei fala para legendar"), then demoCaptions | 5 brief captions over 0–12 s | — | captions where nobody speaks |
| First edit, then Undo, then "Editar com IA" again | 1st Whisper (9 real); **2nd demoCaptions** (7 brief), no Whisper attempt | — | — | — |
| Mock Claude (status configured:true, badge "Claude"): Pular at first edit, then chat "coloque legenda no vídeo" + Pular | generateCaptions → demoCaptions | 7 brief captions, "Coloquei 7 legendas de exemplo… (sem transcrição desta vez)" | 96% | none |
| Mock Claude + CC off, then chat "coloque legenda no vídeo" | demoCaptions | same 7 (no question asked) | — | — |
| Mock Claude, Undo, re-run | 2nd `/api/ai/edit` body had `captions: []` (1st had 9) | — | — | — |

Result files: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/aa48c5f3-da7a-51ea-a4c5-276a3a3dd31a/scratchpad/diag/captions-src/result-*.json`. Script: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/aa48c5f3-da7a-51ea-a4c5-276a3a3dd31a/scratchpad/diag/captions-src/sim.js`.

Caveats:
- WebGPU could not be tested: headless Chromium had no adapter, so the fp16/q4f16 path many Androids take is untested.
- The `.next` build was replaced by another session at 15:30:38. All mobile runs finished before that (latest 15:29:46). The desktop and re-run checks ran after restarting my server on the new build, but the caption code is unchanged.
- The desktop login input is `visibility:hidden` at 1440 px, so I logged in through the mobile layout and reused the cookie. That is a side observation for QA.

## 3. Most likely scenario on Bruno's phone
- Before c3c7dac, `getStatus()` cached a failed check as `{configured:false}` for the whole session (see the c3c7dac diff of client.ts). So the stuck "Demo" badge means `runFirstEdit` took the demo branch (pipeline.ts:302).
- In that branch, any Whisper outcome other than "segments found" produces captions made of his own brief's words, spread evenly over the sound ranges. That matches both complaints exactly: "não tem nada a ver com o que a pessoa fala" and "não segue o ritmo".
- A working Whisper, even tiny, gives mostly-correct text with gaps on the pauses, which doesn't fit "nada a ver".
- Plausible triggers on his phone, which his chat log would tell apart:
  - "Pular legendas" on a device counted as weak.
  - The 41–63 MB model download from huggingface.co failing or stalling on the same flaky connection that broke `/api/ai/status`.
  - CC off.
  - **Re-running the first edit after Undo** (no log line at all).
- After c3c7dac, with Claude active, path B still produces the same brief text if he skipped or had CC off during "Coloque legenda no vídeo".
- Contributing factor: whisper-tiny garbles words (26.9% vs 9.6% for base).

## 4. Proposed policy
**Captions come only from a real transcription of this media.** If none is available, put no caption text on screen, say why, and offer to retry, turn CC on, or write manually.
- Remove A, B and C.
- Cache successful transcripts per asset instead of the tried-once Set.
- Server guard on D and E: Claude can only re-segment or retime existing transcript words; it can fix words only on explicit request and must keep the timings.
- Prompt rule plus `captions.transcribed` flag in the summary.
- Additive `Captions.source` provenance, and detection of the fake captions already saved in IndexedDB.
- whisper-base on capable phones, plus degenerate-output detection.
- Stop copying the reference video's on-screen text into the user's video.
- E2E checks with the Piper fixture: WER < 35%, pauses aligned, the brief's words never in captions.

findings.summary: I measured the in-browser Whisper on a Portuguese test set with known text: 13 clips, about 7 minutes. It used transformers.js 4.3.2, the same version the app loads, with the exact options from lib/ai/whisper.worker.ts and the app's own splitPoints/speechLikely/wordsToSegments code. The model a phone gets on the WASM path, whisper-tiny q8, is not usable for Portuguese. Under background music it produces nonsense: 89.8% WER at 10 dB SNR ("sejam gostos de sejam gostas..."). On one real human clip it falls into a counting loop ("Basta lá, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6...") and outputs 119 words where 44 were spoken (WER 204%). On music with no speech at all, every model invents text: base 58 junk words, small a YouTube-outro sentence. That matches Bruno's report that the captions have "nothing to do" with the speech. whisper-base is acceptable only on clean speech (5.8% WER on synthetic voices, 19.9% on real voices, 35% under music). whisper-small (2.6% / 9.3% / 17%) and large-v3-turbo (1.1% / 5.0% / 11%) are the first models good enough for captions. Word start times are good on base and above, typically 0.06–0.15 s after the measured energy onset. But the last word before a pause is stretched until the next token, so captions stay on screen up to 1.9 s into silences. Turbo does not have this problem. The max_new_tokens=220 limit did not cut anything off even at 4.6 words/s. The real accuracy killers are: the tiny model; q8 quantisation of tiny; a speechLikely gate that lets music through but drops chunks with less than about 5 s of speech per 60 s; no filter against hallucinated text; no voice-activity detection (VAD) to drop words where nobody is speaking; and stretched word end times. On this 4-core x86 box with production settings (WASM, single thread, because the site has no cross-origin isolation headers), measured speed is tiny 0.34–0.43× real time, base 0.58–0.70× and small 1.27–1.75×. On a mid-range Android CPU I expect, as an unmeasured hypothesis, small on WASM to be impractical (roughly 3–6× real time). Recommended policy: WebGPU → whisper-small (or turbo on strong devices); WASM-only phones → base plus VAD and filters, or server-side transcription; never tiny.

rootCauses.claim: Phones get whisper-tiny. On the WASM path, tiny with q8 quantisation is catastrophically inaccurate for Portuguese: it loops and invents text, which produces captions unrelated to what was said.
rootCauses.evidence: lib/ai/whisper.ts:42-48: small = dev.mobile || dev.weak gives 'tiny'; the WASM path uses dtype q8. Measured with the exact worker options: tiny q8 got C_music10 WER 89.8% (output 'É legal que simplesmente invussemos a gente sejam gostos de sejam gostas de sejam...'), C_music3 71.4%, real human R_4367 WER 204.5% (44 words spoken, 119 output, 'Basta lá, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 5, 7...'), pooled real-human WER 80.7%, clean synthetic 18.4%. Greedy decoding is deterministic: it reproduced identically on a rerun. Same clips with base q8: 34.7% / 34.7% / 20.5%, real 19.9%, clean 5.8%. Small q8: 12.2% / 22.4% / 15.9%, real 9.3%, clean 2.6%. large-v3-turbo q8: 10.2% / 12.2% / 4.5%, real 5.0%, clean 1.1%.

rootCauses.claim: The tiny model's errors are made worse by q8 quantisation. The WebGPU dtype mix (fp16 encoder + q4f16 decoder) and fp32 are clearly better but still too weak for captions.
rootCauses.evidence: Tiny with {encoder fp16, decoder q4f16}: music 42.9% / 38.8%, R_4367 27.3%, pooled real 29.8%, clean 18.7%. Tiny fp32: music 53.1% / 42.9%, real 26.7%. Tiny q8: music 89.8% / 71.4%, real 80.7%. Base with the GPU mix: real 16.8%, music 34.7% / 26.5% (close to base q8).

rootCauses.claim: Sections with only music get hallucinated captions. speechLikely does not reject pulsed or beat music, and nothing filters hallucinated text.
rootCauses.evidence: gate.mjs: speechLikely(music only) = true; speech plus music at -5 dB SNR = true; speech plus white noise at 0 dB = true. On a 20 s music-only clip (N_music_only): tiny output 'E aí!'; base 58 words ('e o que é o que é que é o e o que não é...'); small 'Ainda não tem mais um vídeo para mais vídeos, mas eu espero que tenham gostado!'. grep for 'amara|obrigado por assistir|alucina' in lib/ finds only a comment at words.ts:75. sanitizeTranscript (sanitize.ts:285-345) has no blocklist and no words-per-second or repetition check.

rootCauses.claim: speechLikely drops real speech when a 60 s chunk contains less than about 4.8 s of speech, so that whole minute gets no captions.
rootCauses.evidence: words.ts:319-320: loud.length < rms.length*0.08 returns false. gate.mjs: 2 s of speech inside 60 s gives false; 4 s of speech inside 60 s gives false. The chunk is skipped at whisper.ts:148. Very quiet speech (RMS 0.0015, peak below 0.005) is also rejected at words.ts:318.

rootCauses.claim: Captions do not follow the speaker's rhythm at pauses. transformers.js sets each word's end to the next token's timestamp, so the last word before a pause stretches into the silence, often ending exactly on a whole second.
rootCauses.evidence: transformers src/models/whisper/tokenization_whisper.js ~L241-250: end_time = token_timestamps[i+1]. D_pauses with small q8: 'consistência.' runs 5.72–8.00 but speech ends at 6.37 (VAD); 'também.' 19.56–21.00 vs 19.76; tiny 'subir.' 12.10–14.00 vs 12.11. Caption overhang into pauses of 0.5 s or more (19 pauses): tiny max 1.89 s, small median 0.44 s / p90 1.28 s / max 1.63 s, covering more than half the pause in 10 of 19. large-v3-turbo: median 0.00, max 0.10, 0 of 19. Capping word duration at max(0.3, 0.075*chars+0.25) cut small's max from 1.63 s to 0.55 s and p90 from 1.28 s to 0.50 s.

rootCauses.claim: Word start times are reliable for base and larger models; tiny is noticeably late or wrong.
rootCauses.evidence: Error from energy onset (after silences of 0.25 s or more) to the nearest word start, clean clips: base median 0.08–0.15 s, systematically late by +0.08 to +0.15 s, 93–100% within 300 ms; small and turbo similar (0.08–0.17 s). Tiny median 0.17–0.33 s and only 25–50% within 300 ms on real voices. First word of each sentence vs its true start: base median 0.08–0.16 s, tiny 0.16–0.69 s (C_music10 max 1.89 s).

rootCauses.claim: max_new_tokens=220 is not currently a truncation problem. Headroom is thin above about 5 words/s, because in 4.3.2 return_timestamps:'word' also generates segment timestamp tokens.
rootCauses.evidence: Whisper tokenizer gives about 1.3–1.7 tokens per Portuguese word including punctuation; B_vfast (4.61 words/s, 146 words) needs about 200 text tokens per 30 s window. Running B_vfast and B_fast30 with 220 vs 440 tokens gave identical word counts for tiny, base and small (152/152, 154/154, 149/149). transformers ASR pipeline L208-210 sets generation return_timestamps=true for 'word', so timestamp tokens also count toward the 220. Estimate: 5.5 words/s ≈ 289 tokens per 30 s, which would truncate.

rootCauses.claim: In production, WASM runs single-threaded because the site has no COOP/COEP headers, so transcription on phones without WebGPU is slow. That is the reason tiny was chosen, and tiny is the reason for the garbage captions.
rootCauses.evidence: grep finds no Cross-Origin-Opener/Embedder-Policy headers in next.config/middleware. Chromium benchmark on the same jsDelivr 4.3.2 build: not isolated gives crossOriginIsolated=false, numThreads=1. RTF on this 4-core x86 box: tiny 0.34 / 0.43, base 0.58 / 0.70, small 1.27 / 1.75 (A_intro / E_long). With COOP/COEP (credentialless): 2 threads, tiny 0.31 / 0.38, base 0.42 / 0.55. Download (q8): tiny 40.8 MB, base 76.9 MB, small 249 MB, turbo 1085 MB. WebGPU mix: tiny 62.5 MB, base 109.8 MB, small 322 MB, turbo encoder q4f16 370 MB + decoder q4f16 194 MB = 564 MB.

rootCauses.claim: Audio preparation and language forcing are not accuracy problems.
rootCauses.evidence: toMono16k (analysis.ts:52-62) uses OfflineAudioContext(1, len, 16000): the browser's anti-aliasing resampler, with spec stereo-to-mono = 0.5(L+R). decodeAudio first resamples to 44.1 kHz (analysis.ts:28), a harmless double resample. whisperLanguage forces 'portuguese' (whisper.ts:22-25). The test pipeline (AAC 48 kHz decoded to 16 kHz mono by ffmpeg) produced clean results with good models. The 60 s split landed in silence (F_concat cut at 56.8 s; the speech ended at 56.79 s), and the merge across 30 s windows lost no words (F_concat turbo WER 0.6%, small 2.8%).

proposals.title: Remove whisper-tiny from the device policy; choose the model by backend
proposals.details: lib/ai/whisper.ts chooseWhisper(): (1) If WebGPU with shader-f16 is available, use onnx-community/whisper-small_timestamped with dtype {encoder_model:'fp16', decoder_model_merged:'q4f16'} (about 322 MB). Desktop or deviceMemory ≥ 8 may use whisper-large-v3-turbo_timestamped {encoder_model:'q4f16', decoder_model_merged:'q4f16'} (about 564 MB). (2) On WASM only, use whisper-base_timestamped q8 (77 MB) at minimum, never tiny. (3) Fix the WebGPU→WASM fallback at whisper.ts:126 so it switches to base q8 (it currently keeps the model name and could keep tiny). Show the download size up front, as the code already does. Expect about 1.5–2.5× real time for base on a mid-range Android CPU (hypothesis, scaled from the measured 0.58–0.70× on x86 single-thread); offer the server option below for long videos.

proposals.title: Replace the speechLikely gate with real VAD (Silero) and drop words outside speech
proposals.details: Add onnx-community/silero-vad (model_int8.onnx is 0.64 MB, runs in the same transformers.js/onnxruntime worker). Use it to (a) cut chunks at real speech boundaries instead of splitPoints' quietest point, (b) skip regions without speech instead of whole 60 s pieces (fixes the measured drop when a minute holds less than about 4.8 s of speech, words.ts:319-320), and (c) after transcription, discard any word whose [start, end] mostly falls outside VAD speech regions. That removes the hallucinations over music only (tiny 'E aí!', base 58 junk words, small 'espero que tenham gostado'). If VAD is not added immediately, at least change speechLikely to judge speech fraction against the speech duration and not the 60 s window, and stop gating whole pieces.

proposals.title: Filter hallucinations in wordsToSegments / sanitizeTranscript
proposals.details: lib/ai/words.ts / sanitize.ts: (1) Blocklist of known Portuguese Whisper hallucinations, normalised: 'legendas pela comunidade amara.org', 'obrigado por assistir', 'inscreva-se no canal', 'se inscreva', 'espero que tenham gostado', 'até o próximo vídeo', 'tchau tchau', 'legenda adriana zanotto', 'e aí' when alone in a segment. Drop a segment if it matches and the speech region under it is short or musical. (2) Loop detector: drop runs where any 1–3-gram repeats 3 or more times within 10 words, or where words per second exceed 6.5 over 2 s or more (tiny's '1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 5, 7...' and 'sejam gostos de sejam'). no_repeat_ngram_size=4 did not stop either loop. (3) Drop segments where 80% or more of the tokens are digits or punctuation.

proposals.title: Clamp word end times so captions leave the screen when the speaker pauses
proposals.details: lib/ai/words.ts wordsToSegments(): before grouping, clamp each word end to min(original end, start + max(0.3, 0.075*letters + 0.25)). Better, clamp to the VAD or energy offset (last frame above threshold + 0.12 s). Measured on small q8: caption overhang into pauses max 1.63 s → 0.55 s, p90 1.28 s → 0.50 s with the character cap alone. Also split segments at punctuation or pauses before the 7-word / 3.6 s cap where possible (it currently splits 'Eu acho que o mais importante é' | 'a consistência.').

proposals.title: Give WASM threads: cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP credentialless)
proposals.details: Send 'Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin' and 'Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: credentialless' (next.config headers for / and the worker; the shell/infra owner must approve because it affects embeds, blob URLs and CDN imports). This turns on onnxruntime-web WASM multithreading (measured: numThreads 1 → 2 on 4 cores; base RTF 0.58 → 0.42 on A_intro, 0.70 → 0.55 on E_long). Optionally set env.backends.onnx.wasm.numThreads = min(4, hardwareConcurrency-1) in whisper.worker.ts. Check that the jsDelivr imports and HF model fetches still load under COEP credentialless; they did in the local Chromium test.

proposals.title: Raise max_new_tokens and make it depend on the window
proposals.details: lib/ai/whisper.worker.ts:223: in 4.3.2, 'word' timestamps also generate segment timestamp tokens, and Portuguese uses about 1.45 tokens per word. 220 tokens covers about 5 words/s; fast creators reach 5–5.5 words/s (about 260–290 tokens per 30 s). Use max_new_tokens: 400 (Whisper's 448 total minus the prompt). The loop protection should come from the hallucination filter above, not this cap. Measured: no WER change at 4.6 words/s between 220 and 440, runtime about +15–50% only when the model actually loops.

proposals.title: Server-side transcription option for weak phones and long videos
proposals.details: Add /api/ai/transcribe (server) using a hosted large-v3-turbo-class model, for example Groq/OpenAI Whisper APIs with word timestamps, behind an env key. Use it when deviceProfile().mobile && !webgpu, or when the audio is longer than about 3 minutes. On-device WASM small is about 3–6× real time on mid-range Android (hypothesis based on measured x86 single-thread RTF 1.27–1.75), and base is still about 20% WER on real voices and 35% under music. Turbo-class quality measured here: 5.0% real, 11% music, near-zero caption overhang.

proposals.title: Never apply demo/example captions as if they were a transcription
proposals.details: Not Whisper accuracy, but the same symptom. generateCaptions (pipeline.ts:363-372), the demo planFirstEdit (demo.ts:597-602) and the demo chat (demo.ts:823-824) apply demoCaptions(): text drawn from the brief's word pool placed over the speech ranges. That happens whenever Whisper is skipped or fails without a warning, or when the status is stale 'demo'. The result is captions literally unrelated to the speech. Show an error or ask instead.

findings.report:
## Whisper accuracy on Portuguese speech in EditorPro

I ran transformers.js 4.3.2 in Node (onnxruntime-node CPU), the same version the app loads from jsDelivr, using the exact options from `lib/ai/whisper.worker.ts:216-225`. I also reused the app's own chunking and grouping code (`splitPoints`, `speechLikely` and `wordsToSegments`, bundled straight from `lib/ai/words.ts` with esbuild). On top of that I timed the same build in Chromium on the WASM backend.

All files are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/aa48c5f3-da7a-51ea-a4c5-276a3a3dd31a/scratchpad/diag/whisper/`:
- scripts: `synth*.py`, `run.mjs`, `analyze.py`, `capt.py`, `capfix.mjs`, `gate.mjs`, `tok.mjs`, `web/bench.js`
- data: `manifest.json`, `results/*.json`

No repository files were edited.

### Network reachability
| Host | Status |
|---|---|
| huggingface.co | 200 |
| cdn.jsdelivr.net (transformers@4.3.2) | 200 |
| datasets-server | 500 for FLEURS, 200 for MLS |
| PyPI | 200 |
| npm registry | 200 |

### Test set (known text)
- **Synthetic voices:** Piper 1.8 with the pt_BR voices faber, cadu and jeff (medium), downloaded from HF `rhasspy/piper-voices`. Each clip went through AAC 48 kHz encoding and was decoded to 16 kHz mono, like audio from a video file.
  - A_intro: 21.5 s, 3.16 words/s, creator intro
  - B_fast: 34.1 s, 3.84 words/s
  - B_fast30: 27.6 s, 4.17 words/s
  - B_vfast: 31.4 s, 4.61 words/s
  - C_music10 / C_music3: 17.5 s, synthetic pop track (chords, bass, kick, hi-hat) at 10 dB and 3 dB speech-to-music ratio
  - D_pauses: 21.8 s, pauses of 1.0–3.5 s
  - E_long: 57.4 s
  - F_concat: 113 s, exercises the 60 s split and the 30 s windows
  - N_music_only: 20 s of music, no speech
  - N_intro_music: 12 s music, then one sentence
- **Real human voices:** four LibriVox clips from MLS Portuguese with modern spelling (13.8–19.7 s): R_12249…, R_5677…, R_4367…, R_9958….
- **WER:** "lenient" lowercases, removes punctuation and accents, converts digits to words, and maps pra→para, pro→para o.

### Accuracy (lenient WER, same clip set for all models; B_vfast and N_* excluded)
| Model / dtype | Clean synthetic | Music 10 dB / 3 dB | Real voices (pooled) | 113 s clip | Worst case |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tiny q8 (phone WASM path today) | 18.4% | **89.8% / 71.4%** | **80.7%** | 15.3% | R_4367: 204% (119 words output for 44 spoken) |
| tiny fp16 encoder + q4f16 decoder (phone WebGPU path today) | 18.7%* | 42.9% / 38.8% | 29.8% | 12.4% | R_12249: 42% |
| tiny fp32 | 16.8%* | 53.1% / 42.9% | 26.7% | 14.4% | |
| base q8 (desktop WASM today) | 5.8% | 34.7% / 34.7% | 19.9% | 7.1% | R_12249: 23.7% |
| base fp16 + q4f16 (desktop WebGPU today) | 6.4%* | 34.7% / 26.5% | 16.8% | 6.8% | |
| small q8 | 2.6% | 12.2% / 22.4% | 9.3% | 2.8% | R_4367: 15.9% |
| large-v3-turbo q8 | 1.1% | 10.2% / 12.2% | 5.0% | 0.6% | |

\* These three runs include B_vfast in the clean-synthetic pool.

**Hallucination examples (greedy decoding, so they are deterministic; reproduced identically on a rerun):**
- tiny q8 on C_music10: "É legal que simplesmente invussemos a gente sejam gostos de sejam gostas de sejam e sejam gostados..."
- tiny q8 on R_4367 (actual speech: "…bastava-me um"): "Basta lá, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 5, 7, 5, 8, …". `no_repeat_ngram_size: 4` does not stop this loop; only `max_new_tokens: 220` bounds it.
- Music only (N_music_only):
  - tiny: "E aí!"
  - base: 58 words ("e o que é o que é que é o e o que não é…")
  - small: "Ainda não tem mais um vídeo para mais vídeos, mas eu espero que tenham gostado!"
- The music-only intro before a sentence (N_intro_music) was handled correctly by all three models.

### Word timing vs. measured speech onsets (10 ms energy VAD on clean clips)
- **Start times:** the gap between each speech onset (after ≥0.25 s of silence) and the nearest word start has a median of 0.08–0.15 s for base, small and turbo. Words are consistently a little late (+0.08 to +0.17 s), and 93–100% fall within 300 ms. Tiny: median 0.17–0.33 s, and only 25–50% within 300 ms on real voices.
- **First word of each sentence vs. its true start:** base median 0.08–0.16 s; tiny median up to 0.69 s, worst 1.89 s (C_music10).
- **End times (mechanism):** in transformers.js each word ends where the next token starts (`tokenization_whisper.js` ~L241-250). So the last word before a pause is stretched across it, often to a whole second:
  - small, D_pauses: "consistência." runs 5.72→8.00 while speech ends at 6.37; "também." 19.56→21.00 vs 19.76
  - tiny: "subir." 12.10→14.00 vs 12.11
- **Caption overhang after `wordsToSegments`, over 19 pauses of 0.5 s or more:**

| Model | Median | p90 | Max | Pauses more than half covered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tiny q8 | 0.34 s | 1.33 s | 1.89 s | 5/19 |
| base q8 | 0.34 s | 0.52 s | 1.24 s | 5/19 |
| small q8 | 0.44 s | 1.28 s | 1.63 s | 10/19 |
| turbo | 0.00 s | 0.02 s | 0.10 s | 0/19 |
| small with simulated word-length cap | 0.40 s | 0.50 s | 0.55 s | 7/19 |
| base with simulated word-length cap | | 0.48 s | 0.55 s | |

### Review of the app's parameters
- **`max_new_tokens: 220`** (`whisper.worker.ts:223`):
  - Portuguese uses 1.28–1.71 Whisper tokens per word including punctuation (`tok.mjs`).
  - In 4.3.2, `'word'` also turns on generation of segment timestamp tokens (ASR pipeline L208-210), and those count toward the 220.
  - Running 220 vs 440 on B_vfast (4.61 words/s) and B_fast30 gave identical output for tiny, base and small. So it does not truncate today.
  - Estimated need: about 263 tokens per 30 s at 5 words/s and about 289 at 5.5 words/s, so very fast speakers could be cut off. Recommendation: 400.
- **60 s chunking** (`whisper.ts:141`, `words.ts:282`): fine. F_concat was cut at 56.8 s, in silence right after the speech ended at 56.79 s. Merging across the 30 s windows with 5 s stride lost no words (turbo 0.6%, small 2.8% WER on 354 words).
- **`speechLikely`** (`words.ts:308-328`): fails in both directions.
  - Lets non-speech through: pulsed music alone → true; speech + music at -5 dB → true; white noise at 0 dB → true.
  - Rejects real speech: 2 s or 4 s of speech inside a 60 s chunk → false (threshold `loud >= 8%` of the window, about 4.8 s). Quiet speech with peak below 0.005 is also rejected.
- **Language:** forced to `'portuguese'` (`whisper.ts:22-25`). Correct.
- **`toMono16k`** (`analysis.ts:52-62`): OfflineAudioContext at 16 kHz with the browser's anti-aliasing resampler and spec down-mix 0.5(L+R). Correct. `decodeAudio` first resamples to 44.1 kHz (`analysis.ts:28`): a double resample, but harmless.
- **No hallucination filtering anywhere:** `grep -rni "amara|obrigado por assistir|alucina" lib/` only finds a comment at `words.ts:75`, and `sanitizeTranscript` has no text filtering.
- **WebGPU fallback** (`whisper.ts:126`): falls back to WASM q8 with the same model name. If the phone was on tiny, the fallback lands on tiny q8, the worst configuration measured.
- **dtype files:** the WebGPU dtype mix files exist on HF for tiny, base and small (`decoder_model_merged_q4f16.onnx` returns 200).

### Speed and download size
**Chromium WASM** (same jsDelivr 4.3.2 build, 4-core x86 container), with the site served like production (no COOP/COEP, `crossOriginIsolated = false`, `numThreads = 1`):

| Model | RTF A_intro | RTF E_long | Load |
|---|---|---|---|
| tiny q8 | 0.34 | 0.43 | 3.7 s |
| base q8 | 0.58 | 0.70 | 4.5 s |
| small q8 | 1.27 | 1.75 | 7.3 s |

With COOP/COEP set: 2 threads; tiny 0.31 / 0.38, base 0.42 / 0.55.

**Node CPU, 4 threads** (some runs overlapped): tiny ~0.25–0.32, base ~0.28–0.54, small ~0.56–0.74, turbo q8 ~0.91.

**Download sizes (first use):**

| Model | q8 | WebGPU mix |
|---|---|---|
| tiny | 40.8 MB | 62.5 MB |
| base | 76.9 MB | 109.8 MB |
| small | 249 MB | 322 MB |
| turbo | 1085 MB | 564 MB (q4f16 encoder 370 + decoder 194) |
| medium | 986 MB | |

### Conclusion: which model on which device
- **Never use tiny.** On the most realistic inputs (real voices, background music) it produces captions unrelated to what was said. That is exactly Bruno's complaint, and the phone is the device that gets tiny (`whisper.ts:42-48`).
- **Phone with WebGPU + shader-f16** (Chrome on Android 12+ with Adreno or Mali GPUs; *hypothesis*, availability varies by device and I could not test on a real GPU here): use whisper-small with fp16 encoder + q4f16 decoder (322 MB, about 9% WER on real voices and 12–22% under music). Keep the download prompt. Use large-v3-turbo q4f16 only on strong devices or desktop.
- **Phone with WASM only:** base q8 at minimum (77 MB; about 20% real-voice WER, 35% under music). Expected about 1.5–2.5× real time on a mid-range Android CPU (*hypothesis*, scaled from the measured 0.58–0.70 single-thread x86 RTF). Turn on COOP/COEP for threads. Prefer a server-side transcription option for long videos or videos with music.
- **For every model:**
  - Silero VAD (0.64 MB) to gate chunks and drop words outside speech
  - a hallucination blocklist plus loop and words-per-second filters
  - word end times clamped by character count or by the energy offset

findings.summary: Ripple cuts are not the problem. ripple_delete and remove_words carry caption words along with the cut, with zero drift (measured |max| 0.001 s over 79 words, normal and tight cuts alike). The browser preview also draws captions on the playhead clock about 49 ms behind the <video> clock, so the renderer is in sync. Three other causes make captions miss the speaker's rhythm. (1) The word timestamps from transformers.js Whisper (base/small _timestamped, the same call the worker makes) arrive late: word starts about +0.20 s (onsets of breath groups +0.17 s), word ends about +0.24 s, ends of breath groups +0.34 s. Everything downstream inherits this lag: captions and the highlight show up late and stay into the pauses, measured pauses look 0.17 s shorter, and the cuts Claude is told to make from these times (edit-system.md silence rule, remove_words padding 0.03) clip real speech (0.5 s lost in 5 of 6 cuts; remove_words leaves 0.155 s of the target word and removes 0.267 s of the neighbour). Whisper-tiny q8, the model a "weak" phone gets, also dropped 49 of 79 words in my test, so it fails on content as well as timing. (2) The display chunker (engine chunkCaptions) only counts words, inside the arbitrary 7-word / 3.6 s segments that wordsToSegments makes. With maxWords=3 it gives 1-word orphans on screen for 0.19 s (0.02 s with real ASR), chunks that end on articles or prepositions, chunks that straddle breath pauses (words shown about 0.5 s before they are spoken) and blinks between segments. (3) Captions are stored in timeline time and are only moved by ripple_delete. update_clip speed, speedPreset/speedCurve, remove_clip{ripple:true} and move_clip leave them in place (drift up to 1.2 s, 4.3 s and 1.0 s). timemap also ignores speed curves, so a clip transcribed with a curve drifts up to 14.6 s. The fix is in two parts: snap the Whisper times to the audio energy (VAD), which in my prototype cut the bias from +0.22 s to about 0 and the words with more than 0.15 s error from 40 to 5; then replace count-only chunking with a DP chunker that breaks on pauses, cut points and punctuation and avoids articles/prepositions. On the same data the prototype brought chunks mixing breath groups from 10 to 0, blinks from 6 to 0 and orphans from 3 to 0, with a minimum on-screen time of 0.42 s instead of 0.19 s.

proposals.title: Snap Whisper word times to the audio (VAD) and auto-calibrate the lag
proposals.details:
New pure function in lib/ai/words.ts: refineWordTimes(chunks: WhisperChunk[], samples16k: Float32Array): WhisperChunk[], called in lib/ai/whisper.ts transcribeMedia before wordsToSegments (local and server paths; on the server path the estimated lag should be about 0, so it is harmless).

Algorithm, as validated in the prototype:
1. RMS dB over 10 ms hops. Threshold = clamp(floor + 0.3·(p90 − floor), −60, −18), the same formula as detectSilences, with floor = p10. Bridge unvoiced gaps under 80 ms and drop islands under 50 ms, giving speech runs [on, off].
2. lag = median(w.start − onset) over words whose start falls within [onset − 0.05, onset + 0.45] of some run onset; clamp to [0, 0.4]; use 0 if fewer than 3 samples.
3. For each word: s = start − lag, e = end − lag. Snap s to the nearest onset within ±0.15 s and e to the nearest offset within ±0.25 s.
4. Enforce monotonic order: s_i ≥ s_{i−1} + 0.06, e_i ≥ s_i + 0.06, then trim e_{i−1} to s_i.
5. Zero or null ends get e = s + max(0.12, 0.06·chars).

Measured on whisper-base: START bias +0.223 → +0.015 s and END +0.254 → +0.005 s; words with error >0.15 s 40 → 5 (start) and 45 → 4 (end).

Add a vitest case with synthetic samples (tone bursts with known onsets plus chunks shifted by 0.2 s).

proposals.title: Rhythm-aware caption chunker in the engine (replace count-only chunkCaptions)
proposals.details:
lib/engine/captions.ts: chunkCaptions(segments, maxWords) becomes chunkCaptions(segments, opts: RhythmOpts | number); a number keeps backward compatibility. It works on the FLAT word list across segments (a segment boundary is just a strong break candidate) and takes the edit cut points (video clip starts > 0) as an extra input. The prototype is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/aa48c5f3-da7a-51ea-a4c5-276a3a3dd31a/scratchpad/diag/captions-rhythm/rhythm.ts.

Break score between words a and b (gap = b.start − a.end; lower is a better place to break):
- Mandatory break if gap ≥ hardGap or a ends with [.!?…].
- −3 if an edit cut lies in the gap. After a demo cut only 2·pad = 0.24 s of pause remains, so a pause threshold alone would miss these.
- If gap ≥ pauseBreak: −(4 + 6·min(1, (gap − pauseBreak)/0.3)). Else if gap ≥ 0.12: −2·(gap − 0.12)/(pauseBreak − 0.12).
- −3 if a ends with , ; : —
- −1 if b starts a clause (e, mas, porque, então, quando, se, ou, que, depois, agora…).
- +4 if a is a glue word (articles, prepositions/contractions, clitics, possessives, 'que', 'e', short auxiliaries like vou/vai/tá).
- +5 if a is a number and b is a unit ('%', por cento, reais, mil, vezes, anos…).

Dynamic programming over the chunk [i..j):
- Infeasible if n > maxWords, chars > maxChars or dur > maxDur (a single word is always allowed).
- cost = best[i] + 0.6·(target − n)², with target = min(maxWords, 3).
- Plus the break score at j (−12 when the break is mandatory).
- +3 for a one-word chunk under 0.35 s when maxWords ≥ 2 and the word is neither emphasized nor isolated by mandatory breaks on both sides.

Timing:
- start = max(prev.end, firstWord.start − leadIn).
- end = min(next.firstWord.start − leadIn, lastWord.end + tailHold).
- If the gap to the next chunk is < closeGap, set end = next start (no blink).
- If end − start < minOn, extend to min(next start, start + minOn).

Highlight: keep wordStates' 'last word whose start passed' rule. Optionally light the word 0.03 s early, since the eye leads the ear.

Measured, maxWords=3, synthetic creator speech:
- chunks mixing breath groups 10 → 0
- chunks ending on an article/preposition 13 → 2
- one-word orphans under 0.3 s 3 → 0
- blinks under 0.2 s 6 → 0
- words shown early across a pause 10 → 0
- minimum on-screen 0.19 → 0.42 s

Whisper-base input: mix 7 → 0, orphans 6 → 1, blinks 1 → 0. Keep the WeakMap cache in textDraw.ts cachedChunks, keyed by segments plus opts plus cut list.

proposals.title: Style presets choose the chunk rhythm (additive contract field)
proposals.details:
lib/types.ts gets an optional CaptionStyle.rhythm?: 'word'|'punch'|'line'|'phrase' plus chunking?: Partial<RhythmOpts>. sanitizeCaptionStyle accepts it, and StyleProfile.captions can carry it from the reference analysis (prompts/analyze-reference.md asks how many words are on screen at once).

Defaults, from the prototype:
- word (stomp / single-word): maxWords 1, maxChars 14, maxDur 1.2, pauseBreak 0.20, hardGap 0.5, minOn 0.22, leadIn 0.05, tailHold 0.20, closeGap 0.20. Also allow a glue word ('de', 'a', 'o') to merge with the next word into 2 words when the pair is under 0.45 s.
- punch (bold-pop / creator / impacto, the default for TikTok/Reels): maxWords 3, maxChars 18, maxDur 1.8, pauseBreak 0.20, hardGap 0.5, minOn 0.40, leadIn 0.06, tailHold 0.25, closeGap 0.25.
- line (karaoke / boxed / caixa-por-palavra): maxWords 4, maxChars 26, maxDur 2.4, pauseBreak 0.25, hardGap 0.6, minOn 0.50, leadIn 0.06, tailHold 0.30, closeGap 0.30.

When rhythm is absent, derive it from maxWords (1 → word, 2–3 → punch, 4–5 → line, 6+ → phrase) so existing presets (components/panels/presets.ts, lib/library/captionsMore.ts) keep working. Scale maxChars by fontSize/lines (≈ 0.84·W / (0.55·fontPx) per line).

### Experiment 1: pipeline drift with exact word times (`pipeline.exp.ts`)
Input: synthetic creator speech, 79 words, 42.3 s, breath pauses 0.22–0.50 s, sentence pauses 0.7–1.6 s.

| Step | Word-start drift, caption − speech |
|---|---|
| After set_captions | ≤0.001 s |
| After 8 demo silence cuts (6.5 s removed) | ≤0.001 s |
| After tight cuts (min 0.3, pad 0.05) | ≤0.001 s |

Ops applied after the cuts (drift = caption − true timeline time):

| Op | Drift |
|---|---|
| update_clip speed 1.2 on all clips | mean +0.455, max 1.231 s |
| speedPreset hero on 1 clip | max 1.170 s |
| remove_clip ripple | 68 words off by 4.283 s |
| move_clip +1 s | 1.001 s |
| trim_clip head | OK |
| Clip already had speedPreset montage when transcribed (timemap ignores the curve) | mean 8.33 s, max 14.62 s |
| Clip at constant speed 1.5 when transcribed | OK |

Engine chunks (maxWords=3), on the same speech:
- 32 chunks, minimum on-screen 0.19 s
- 10 chunks mix two breath groups
- 12–13 end on an article or preposition
- 3 one-word orphans
- 6–12 blank gaps under 0.2–0.25 s (the threshold differs between the two metrics)

The first 14 chunks:

`[Você sabia que] [noventa por cento] [das] [pessoas erram isso] [na hora de] [editar?] [Eu vou te] [mostrar agora o] [truque] [que mudou meu] [canal.] [Primeiro, grava sempre] [na vertical, com] [a]`

Highlight check, sampled at 60 fps: 0 wrong active words in 1623 speaking frames, and no blank frames while speech is happening.

### Experiment 2: real Whisper timing accuracy (`asr/`)
**Setup**
- Speech: espeak-ng pt-br through ctypes; WORD events give the ground-truth word times.
- Pauses: breath 0.25–0.45 s, sentence 0.8–1.4 s; total 36.4 s.
- ASR: transformers.js 4.3.2 in Node, dtype q8, the same pipeline options as the worker, pieces from splitPoints.

**Content accuracy** (exact matches out of 79 words):
- tiny: 30 words output, 11 matched
- base: 56 matched
- small: 54 matched

**Timing error, base:**
- word START mean +0.223 s, median +0.196, p90 0.341
- word END mean +0.254 s
- onsets of breath groups: +0.170 s median (min +0.082)
- ends of breath groups: +0.339 s
- small is identical
- pauses measured by the ASR are 0.173 s shorter than the real ones

**After VAD snapping** (`refine.py`, estimated lag +0.220 s from 34 onsets):
- START error +0.015 s; words >0.15 s off: 5
- END error +0.005 s; words >0.15 s off: 4

**What the late times do to cuts** made by the prompt rules:

| Rule | Raw times | Snapped times |
|---|---|---|
| Silence rule ±0.12 | 5 of 6 cuts eat speech, 0.500 s total | 1 cut, 0.165 s |
| remove_words, padding 0.03 | median 0.155 s of the target word left, 0.267 s of the neighbour removed | 0.020 s left, 0.053 s removed |

**Through the real pipeline** (`real.exp.ts`: detectSilences on the audio found 8 cuts; no real words were lost):
- The chunk holding a breath group's first word appears at median +0.113 s, max +0.326 s. With exact times it appears on time.
- With exact times, chunks that straddle a pause show words up to 0.5 s early.

### Experiment 3: real browser (`browser.js`, `/dev/preview` on port 3104, `talk.mp4` with the espeak audio, base segments plus the real detectSilences ripple ops)
- Playhead (the caption clock) minus the `<video>` currentTime mapped to the timeline: median −0.049 s, p05 −0.062, p95 −0.035 (n=1336). The renderer is in sync to about 50 ms.
- Caption pixels matched the engine's expectation in 1378 of 1421 frames. The 43 misses are at chunk starts, where the pop animation's opacity is still ramping up.
- The screenshot shows a one-word orphan chunk "OU".
- Side finding: a 0.25 ms sliver clip remains at the end after silenceCutOps.

### Experiment 4: current vs proposed chunker (`compare.exp.ts`, prototype `rhythm.ts`)
Synthetic speech, maxWords=3:

| Metric | Current | Rhythm-aware |
|---|---|---|
| Chunks mixing breath groups | 10 | 0 |
| Ending on an article/preposition | 13 | 2 |
| Orphans under 0.3 s | 3 | 0 |
| Blinks under 0.2 s | 6 | 0 |
| Words shown early across a pause | 10 | 0 |
| Minimum on-screen | 0.19 s | 0.42 s |

Other maxWords values:
- maxWords=7: current mixes breath groups in 9 chunks, rhythm-aware in 0.
- maxWords=2: current ends 15 chunks on an article/preposition, rhythm-aware 8.

Whisper-base input (maxWords=3):
- raw times: mixing 7 → 1, orphans 4 → 1, blinks 1 → 0, minimum on-screen 0.02 → 0.24 s
- snapped times: mixing 7 → 0, orphans 6 → 1

First 16 rhythm-aware chunks:

`[Você sabia] [que noventa] [por cento] [das pessoas] [erram] [isso na hora] [de editar?] [Eu vou te] [mostrar agora] [o truque] [que mudou] [meu canal.] [Primeiro,] [grava sempre] [na vertical,] [com a luz]`

### Proposed algorithm (exact)
**Step 1 — snap word times to the audio (refineWordTimes), before segmentation:**
- RMS over 10 ms hops; adaptive threshold `clamp(p10 + 0.3·(p90 − p10), −60, −18)` dB; bridge gaps under 80 ms; drop islands under 50 ms.
- lag = median(start − onset) over words within [−0.05, +0.45] s of an onset; clamp to [0, 0.4].
- Shift every word by −lag. Snap starts to an onset within ±0.15 s and ends to an offset within ±0.25 s.
- Keep the order monotonic with at least 0.06 s per word.

**Step 2 — segments:** wordsToSegments at maxWords 12, maxDur 6, pauseGap 0.45. Segments become phrases or sentences.

**Step 3 — engine chunks:** dynamic programming over the flat word list. Inputs are the break scores (pause, edit cut, punctuation, clause start, articles/prepositions, number + unit), the per-style limits (maxWords, maxChars, maxDur) and an orphan penalty. On-screen timing:
- start = firstWord.start − leadIn
- end = lastWord.end + tailHold, capped at the next chunk's start
- gaps shorter than closeGap are closed
- minimum on-screen time minOn

**Step 4 — style presets:** word / punch / line / phrase. The parameter values are in the proposals.

**Step 5 — keep captions anchored to the media:** retime them for speed, speed curve, remove_clip ripple and move_clip, and fix the curve handling in timemap.

**Step 6 — AI cuts:** snap them to measured silences instead of trusting the raw Whisper edges.

### Caveats
- espeak is a robotic TTS voice. The +0.17–0.22 s lag agrees across base and small and is measured against exact onsets, but its size on real human voice is still a hypothesis until it is checked on a real recording. The VAD snap handles any size of lag because it estimates the lag from the audio itself.
- Real recordings have noise floors. The adaptive threshold is the same one detectSilences already relies on in demo mode.

findings.summary: The main finding is about configuration, not missing code. The server-side, high-accuracy transcription path is already built and deployed: app/api/ai/transcribe/route.ts and lib/ai/server/transcribe.ts send 16 kHz mono WAV chunks to Groq whisper-large-v3-turbo, or to OpenAI whisper-1, and ask for word timestamps (commit d6d4afc, which is on origin/claude/ai-video-editor-r0tr67). It is switched off in production because the Vercel project editor-pro has no GROQ_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY; its only env vars are ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, DASH_PASSWORD and ANTHROPIC_MODEL. So /api/ai/status returns transcribe:null. Every phone run therefore uses in-browser Whisper: base q8 over WASM, or tiny when deviceMemory is 2 GB or less. On FLEURS Portuguese those score about 13.9% and 24% WER, against about 3.9–4.1% for large-v3, which fits "the captions don't match what the person says". My recommendation: (1) Groq free tier (no card; the official table shows 2K requests and 28.8K audio-seconds/day, about 8 h/day; $0.04/h after that). The owner adds only GROQ_API_KEY, with zero code changes. (2) Add Cloudflare Workers AI whisper-large-v3-turbo as a second free provider: 10,000 neurons/day ≈ 214 audio-min/day, word timestamps in segments[].words, zero data retention. (3) Deepgram nova-3 pt-BR is optional: a one-time $200 credit that does not expire, about 775 h, with CORS-enabled short-lived tokens so the browser can upload directly and skip the 4.5 MB / 60 s limits. There is no legitimate, reliable free option that needs no key at all. The closest is the Vercel AI Gateway through the deployment's OIDC token, but I could not confirm that transcription models are covered by its $5/30-day free credit.

## Free server-side speech-to-text for PT-BR captions: research report

### 0. Key finding: the server-side path is already built but switched off in production
- `web/app/api/ai/transcribe/route.ts` exists. It accepts `POST ?lang=pt-BR` with an `audio/wav` body, rejects bodies over `MAX_BODY_BYTES = 4_400_000` (`lib/ai/server/http.ts:16`), and sets `runtime='nodejs'` and `maxDuration=60`.
- `web/lib/ai/server/transcribe.ts` sends a multipart request to Groq (`GROQ_API_KEY`, model `whisper-large-v3-turbo`, overridable with `GROQ_TRANSCRIBE_MODEL`) or to OpenAI (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `whisper-1`). The request uses `response_format=verbose_json`, `timestamp_granularities[]=word` and `segment`, `language=pt` and `temperature=0`. If no word timings come back, it spreads segment time evenly across the words.
- The client side (`web/lib/ai/whisper.ts:164-206, 238-255`) works like this:
  - It decodes the audio to 16 kHz mono, cuts it at silences into chunks of at most 100 s, and skips chunks without speech (`speechLikely`).
  - It uploads WAV chunks two at a time and adds each chunk's start offset to the word times.
  - This only happens when `getStatus().transcribe` is truthy. Otherwise it runs `transcribeLocal`.
- **Production has no transcription key.** The Vercel API (`filter_project_envs` on `prj_4ow4vaCopsLqpdQbcUuBrdyRbspF`) returns only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `DASH_PASSWORD` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`. So `/api/ai/status` reports `transcribe: null`, and the phone always runs in-browser Whisper.
- Commit d6d4afc ("legendas: só a fala de verdade…", 2026-11-19 15:48 UTC) is in `origin/claude/ai-video-editor-r0tr67`.

### 1. Accuracy gap (PT-BR, FLEURS WER)
- The Handy leaderboard (Q8 builds) gives whisper-tiny 24.07%, base 13.91%, medium 5.07% and large-v3 3.88%. ElevenLabs reports large-v3 at 4.1%.

### 3. Ranked recommendation
1. **Groq.** It is free, needs no card, and gives about 8 h of audio per day (verify in console). The code is already merged, so the only step is setting GROQ_API_KEY on Vercel and redeploying (exact steps in proposals).
2. **Cloudflare Workers AI** as an automatic second provider when Groq returns 429, using the same large-v3-turbo with word timestamps and about 214 free minutes/day. It needs about 30 lines in `lib/ai/server/transcribe.ts`.
3. **Deepgram nova-3 pt-BR** if the owner wants the best timing and robustness. The $200 credit lasts a single user for years, and the direct browser upload removes the 4.5 MB / 60 s limits.
4. Keep in-browser Whisper as the no-key fallback, with a clear "lower quality" notice on phones.

### 4. Route spec (extends the existing route; repo files were not edited)
- `POST /api/ai/transcribe?lang=pt-BR&offset=<s>`. Body is `audio/webm` (Opus) or `audio/wav`, at most 4.4 MB. Response: `{ text, words:[{word,start,end}], provider }` with times relative to the chunk. Errors: 413 / 400 / 429 (`retryAfter`) / 501 when not configured / 502.
- Provider selection: `TRANSCRIBE_PROVIDER = auto|groq|cloudflare|deepgram|openai`. In `auto`, the first configured provider wins: `GROQ_API_KEY` → (`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` + `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`) → `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` → `OPENAI_API_KEY`. On a 429 or 5xx, the route tries the next configured provider.
- Groq/OpenAI: multipart as today, with filename `audio.webm` or `audio.wav` matching Content-Type.
- Cloudflare: `POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{id}/ai/run/@cf/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo` with Bearer token and JSON `{audio: base64, task:'transcribe', language:'pt', vad_filter:true, condition_on_previous_text:false}` → `result.segments[].words[]`.
- Deepgram (optional): `GET /api/ai/transcribe/token` → `POST https://api.deepgram.com/v1/auth/grant` with `Authorization: Token $DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` and `{ttl_seconds:120}`. The browser then calls `/v1/listen?model=nova-3&language=pt-BR&smart_format=true&punctuate=true&utterances=true&mip_opt_out=true`.
- Auth: the existing `middleware.ts` matcher already covers `/api/ai/:path*` with the HMAC session cookie (401 JSON for API calls). Keys stay server-side only; `/api/ai/status` exposes only the provider name.

### 5. Client spec
- Decode → 16 kHz mono (existing `toMono16k`) → `splitPoints(audio,16000,100,8)` (cuts in silence, so no overlap or dedup is needed) → skip chunks where `speechLikely` is false.
- Encoding: WebCodecs `AudioEncoder` (Opus, mono, 32 kbps) + `webm-muxer` (already in package.json), about 4 KB/s, so a 100 s chunk is ~0.4 MB instead of 3.2 MB of WAV (16000×2×100+44 = 3,200,044 B). Fall back to `encodeWav`. iOS Safari support for AudioEncoder is unverified, hence the fallback.
- Parallelism: 3 concurrent requests (Groq allows 20 RPM). Per chunk, keep the 70 s abort and retry twice with backoff on 429/5xx. If the chunk still fails, transcribe **only that chunk** locally, instead of today's whole-file fallback at `whisper.ts:246-251`.
- Merging: word.start/end are clamped to [0, chunkLen], then `+ chunkStart`. Sort, then force non-decreasing starts. Then the existing `wordsToSegments` → `dropHallucinations` → `captionsMediaToTimeline`.
- Limits check:
  - WAV fits up to 137 s per request (4.4 MB / 32 KB/s); Opus fits about 1100 s.
  - Groq processes at about 216x real time, so a 100 s chunk takes well under 2 s plus upload time, far inside `maxDuration=60`.
  - Each Groq request is billed at least 10 s, which is irrelevant with 100 s chunks.

### 6. Privacy
- Audio leaves the device when server transcription is on. The UI should say so ("áudio enviado ao serviço de transcrição").
- Cloudflare lists zero data retention. For Deepgram, use `mip_opt_out=true`. I did not find Groq's retention policy.
- No key is ever sent to the browser except Deepgram's short-lived JWT.
- Disclosure: one CORS preflight I sent to Deepgram during this research carried the production origin header. Later probes used `https://example.com`.

findings.summary: The reference video is treated as a loose hint, not a template. Locally the app only measures cut times (48x27 frame diffs, sampled every 0.25 s), mean color and aspect ratio. It measures no camera motion, no caption region or style, and no transitions. The demo/local path, which is what Bruno's phone ran while the badge was stuck on "Demo", then makes up the rest from the pacing alone: transitions ['cut','zoom-in'], zoomPunchIns=true, a bold-pop caption style and a 'vibrant' color preset. In a real run, a reference with 10 hard cuts of 1.2 s, smooth eased 15% push-ins, yellow uppercase boxed captions and a warm grade came out as one uncut 15 s clip with abrupt 0.18 s punch zooms (1↔1.16 every 2 s) and the wrong look ('vibrant'). "Reedite seguindo o modelo" did cut every 1.2 s, but it also added zoom-in transitions on all 11 cuts (the reference has only hard cuts), left half the shots frozen at 1.16 with the other half creeping linearly to 1.04, and applied both the 'vibrant' preset and colorGrade. On the Claude path the StyleProfile is too thin to carry the template: one zoom boolean, no cut list, no motion, no color stats, and no reference frames in the edit call. The edit prompt also tells Claude to use transitions "com moderação" and to always add "gancho, zooms, cor, efeitos e transições". A ~100-line prototype (108x192, 10 fps, scale+translation search) recovered the exact cut times, per-shot zoom of 1.12–1.16 and an eased velocity profile, and told smooth (peak/mean 1.5–1.9) apart from punch (13.6). This shows the "modelo definitivo" measurement can be done locally.

proposals.title: Measure reference motion locally (per-shot zoom/pan, speed and smoothness)
proposals.details: New lib/ai/motion.ts (pure + browser sampler), called from sampleReference (lib/ai/analysis.ts). Decode the reference at about 10 fps into 108x192 grayscale via the existing <video>+canvas seek loop (or requestVideoFrameCallback while playing muted at 2x, which is faster than seeking on Android). For each consecutive pair: (1) a coarse search for scale s in [0.97,1.06] (37 steps) about the center, then translation tx,ty in ±3 px, minimizing the masked mean absolute difference (mask out a 12% border and the detected caption band); or log-polar phase correlation for speed. (2) If the residual after alignment is > max(25, median + 8·MAD), mark a cut. This gives exact cut times; the prototype found 1.2…10.8 exactly, against the current output that is up to 0.2 s late. Per shot, output {start, end, zoomTotal = exp(sum(log s)), panX/panY total, velocity profile, peakOverMean, easing class (linear / easeIn / easeOut / easeInOut, from where the velocity peaks), punch events (single-step |log s| > 0.025 with peakOverMean > 4)}. Prototype numbers: reference zoomTotal 1.12–1.16 (truth 1.15), peak/mean 1.5–1.9 = smooth; punch emulation 13.6; static clip 1.000. Budget: ≤ 2 s on desktop for 60 s of reference. Use 6 fps / 72x128 when deviceProfile().weak. Prototype: scratchpad diag/reference/motion.py.

proposals.title: Richer reference profile (additive contract fields)
proposals.details: Add an optional `template?: ReferenceTemplate` to StyleProfile in lib/types.ts (additive): shots: {start,end,dur}[] (the real distribution plus median, p10 and p90), cutsOnBeats ratio (when the reference has audio: run detectBeats on its audio and count cuts within ±80 ms of a beat), motion per shot (above) plus a summary {mode: 'smooth-push'|'punch'|'static'|'pan'|'mixed', avgZoomPerShot, direction in/out ratio, easing}, transitions: measured kinds and frequency (detect dissolve as a ≥3-sample ramp of diffs with mixed content, flash as a luminance spike, whip as a high-motion blur run) with durations, captions: {region:{y0,y1,x0,x1}, textColor, boxColor|null, heightPx1920, uppercase?, wordsPerChunk (from the change rate of the band content vs the speech rate)}, color: the full ColorStats (mean, lumSd, sat) plus a 3x3 RGB matrix or a per-channel 16-bin histogram to drive matchColorGrade. Store it in project.style.template, so the cuts and motion survive to the edit call and later chat turns. Extend sanitizeStyleProfile with clamps for it. Caption region heuristic as prototyped in capdetect.py (temporally static + high-edge band while the background changes; dominant bright vs dark colors). It worked on the reference: band 0.70–0.77, text #F3D205, box #110E0D. It gives a false positive on a fully static background, so gate it on background motion and let Claude confirm.

## 5. Gap list: what is NOT captured or NOT enforced

1. **Pacing**: only the mean shot length survives. There is no distribution, no order, no cut-on-beat or cut-on-word. The demo first edit ignores pacing completely, and the chat restyle splits on a uniform grid regardless of speech.
2. **Camera motion**: not measured, and not representable beyond a boolean. Defaults are abrupt punch-ins (`demo.ts:401-433`). Smooth push or pull, pans, speed ramps, easing and magnitude are all lost. The engine already supports eased keyframes (`lib/engine/easing.ts:41-63`), so this is purely an AI-side gap.
3. **Transitions**: locally invented (zoom-in or crossfade). Claude sees about 1 fps, so 0.25–0.4 s transitions are mostly between samples (hypothesis). The prompt says to moderate them. No duration or frequency is kept.
4. **Caption style**: no local measurement. Demo guesses bold-pop. Claude relies on 1 fps JPEGs at 512 px. Words per chunk is not measured. The style is applied only after segments exist.
5. **Text overlays / hook**: the demo copies the reference's text verbatim (`demo.ts:627`). Claude is told to always add a hook.
6. **B-roll usage, effects, zoom frequency, music energy**: not measured. Music is guessed visually ("sem áudio, deduza pelo ritmo"), and the reference audio is never decoded, although `detectBeats` exists.
7. **Color**: the first edit uses a preset from a heuristic that mislabels warm as vibrant. The measured grade appears only in the chat restyle and stacks with the preset. The Claude analysis never sees the color stats.
8. **Defaults overriding the model**: fast pacing → tiktok captions, zoom punch, zoom-in transitions, fillerOps. `intent.calm` → warm color and crossfade. The Claude task always asks for "gancho, zooms, cor, efeitos e transições".
9. **No fidelity check**: nothing compares the output with the reference. The review pass, where it exists in later code, compares only against the user text.
10. **Bruno's phone context**: with the stale "Demo" status, `sampleReference(..., withFrames=false)` ran, Claude never saw the reference, and everything above is exactly what he got. This is a hypothesis for his session; the mechanism is confirmed.

## 6. "Modelo definitivo" design (summary; details in proposals)

1. **Measure** in `lib/ai/motion.ts`, extending sampleReference:
   - exact cuts plus the shot distribution
   - per-shot zoom and pan magnitude, easing class and punch events
   - transition detection: dissolve ramps, flash luminance spikes, whip motion blur
   - caption band: region, text and box color, size, chunk rate
   - full color stats or histograms
   - reference audio beats, to count cuts on beats
   - stored additively as `StyleProfile.template`
2. **Analyze**:
   - send Claude the measured template, frame pairs around cuts and crops of the caption band
   - richer schema: camera, transitions with frequency and duration, caption box and wordsPerChunk, effects, b-roll
   - measured fields override Claude's estimates
3. **Replicate strictly**:
   - Claude: a "MODELO DEFINITIVO" task with no generic hook, zoom or effects, deterministic rules for shots, camera keyframes with easeInOut, transitions and captions, a pre-computed colorGrade, and reference frames in the edit call
   - demo: `templateOps` (word-gap splits following the reference's shot sequence, eased per-shot moves, measured transitions only, measured caption style, colorGrade only)
4. **Verify**:
   - render the result at about 2 fps and run the same estimators
   - per-aspect fidelity score (pacing, motion smoothness and magnitude, transitions, captions, color)
   - one repair round with the concrete deltas, and a fidelity line in the chat reply

findings.summary: The math in preview and export is correct. A keyframed 1.0→1.2 / 3 s easeInOut zoom exports within 0.2 px of the ideal curve, with no integer snapping and no dropped or duplicated frames. Native and canvas modes compute the same geometry, and the canvas→native switch moved the picture by only 1.2 px. The roughness Bruno sees comes mostly from what the planners generate, not from the renderer. The demo, Claude-recipe and reference-driven paths create punch motion: 0.15–0.18 s ramps to 1.10–1.18, the 1.25→1 hook in 0.5 s, sawtooth pulses that jump in one frame, 24 Hz random shake and static 1/1.12–1.18 jump-cut scales. Measured jumps reach 24–50 px of edge movement per frame at 1080 wide, versus 2–4 px for a cinematic push-in. Separately, the reference-video path cannot represent smooth motion at all. StyleProfile only has `zoomPunchIns: boolean`; analysis samples about 1 frame per second with no motion estimate. The demo and 'apply model' paths turn any fast-paced reference into punch-ins or alternating zoom (jump cuts). Smaller renderer issues: in preview, transforms update only at the project fps (30 Hz on 60/120 Hz screens); native mode animates zoom by changing CSS width/height every frame; geometry effects run on timeline time, not clip time; and there is no smooth-through-keyframes interpolation or motion blur.
