## Smooth motion ("movimentos suaves"): motion in preview and export

Repository files were not changed. Experiment files are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/aa48c5f3-da7a-51ea-a4c5-276a3a3dd31a/scratchpad/diag/motion/`:
- `math.ts`: planner and effect curves, using the real code bundled with esbuild.
- `pv.js`: preview sampler running against the server on port 3106.
- `ex.js` and `fa.py`: export, then per-frame scale measured with ffmpeg.
- `an.py`: analysis of the preview samples.
- `box.mp4`, `test.mp4`: test videos.
- `exp_*.mp4`: exported results.

The server I started on 3106 has been stopped. Another session rebuilt `.next` while I was working, so my measurements ran on the build of HEAD 2bb3fd3.

### Where motion is generated
| Source | File:line | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Keyframe interpolation | lib/engine/easing.ts:8-16, 41-61; lib/engine/animate.ts:107-125 | Each segment uses its own easing. Easing is linear, easeIn, easeOut or easeInOut (cubic); if absent, it is linear. Nothing interpolates smoothly through several keyframes. |
| Emphasis zoom (demo and "zoom na ênfase") | lib/ai/features.ts:132-165 | 1→1.18 in about 0.16 s (easeOut), hold, then back to 1 in 0.25 s (easeInOut). |
| Hook zoom | features.ts:304, prompts/edit-system.md:159 | 1.25→1 in 0.5 s, easeOut. |
| Demo zoom punch-in | lib/ai/demo.ts:401-433 | Single clip: alternates 1↔1.10/1.16 every 2–2.8 s with an 0.18 s ramp. With 3 or more clips: alternating static scale, plus a linear 1→1.04 push. |
| Beat sync | features.ts:210-241 | Static scale alternating 1/1.12 per cut, plus a flash. |
| Applying the reference style | lib/ai/model.ts:113-125 | Cuts at fixed intervals. `if (s.zoomPunchIns or fast) zoomOps` adds alternating zoom. |
| Local reference analysis | demo.ts:205-224 | `zoomPunchIns: fast`, decided by cut rate only. |
| Geometry effects | lib/fx/geometry.ts:18-62; lib/engine/effects.ts:28-43 | zoom-punch, zoom-slow, handheld, shake-3d, beat-pulse, shake, zoom-pulse. All use timeline time `t`. |
| Clip animations | lib/engine/animations.ts, lib/fx/clipAnimations.ts | Intro/outro animations with cubic easeOut. Loops are sinusoidal (smooth). |
| Claude guidance | prompts/edit-system.md:126, 159, 160, 187; prompts/analyze-reference.md:13, 25 | Asks for "keyframes rápidos" and alternating zoom. Nothing about smoothness, minimum durations or mandatory easing. |

### Pure math (real code, edge displacement per frame at 1080 px wide)
| Curve | 30 fps | 60 fps |
|---|---|---|
| (a) keyframe 1.0→1.2 over 3 s, easeInOut | max 3.5 px/frame, peak 0.20 scale/s | 1.8 |
| (a2) same, linear (Claude left easing out) | velocity step 0→0.0022 per frame at start and end | – |
| (b1) emphasis zoom | **42.4 px/frame**: 1.000 1.032 1.110 1.155 1.175 1.180 | 23.8 |
| (b2) hook 1.25→1 in 0.5 s | **25.2 px/frame**: 1.250 1.203 1.163 1.128… | 13.1 |
| (b3/b4) demo punchKeyframes, normal / strong | 24.4 / 39.0 px/frame | – |
| (c1) zoom-punch effect, intensity 0.5 | **33.0 px/frame** (1.000→1.031→1.061→1.092→1.110 in 4 frames at 60 fps) | 16.5 |
| zoom-pulse | 0→6 % in one frame: 1.000 1.000 1.060 1.049 | – |
| beat-pulse | 24.3 px/frame, jumps in one frame | – |
| shake | dx at 60 fps: 8.6 8.6 8.6 −10.7 −10.7 8.1… (random values held at 24 Hz) | – |
| zoom-slow, handheld | 0.8 / 0.3 px/frame (smooth) | – |

### Preview measurement (Playwright on port 3106, box.mp4 at 1080×1920 in a 9:16 project)
Headless Chromium plays H.264, so native mode was active. Headless rAF ran at about 17.5 ms per frame.

- **A, slow zoom, easeInOut, native mode:** 247 rAF samples, 84 geometry updates, 162 rAFs with no change.
  - Update intervals: 33 ms ×76, 50 ms ×6.
  - Mid-ramp edge step per update: 2.06 to 3.93 px (max/min ratio 1.90).
  - `video.currentTime` ran 35–74 ms ahead of the playhead. That doesn't matter for a zoom.
- **D, same zoom forced into canvas mode (vignette):** draw intervals 33 ms ×92, 42 ms ×22, 50 ms ×2; step ratio 2.32.
- **B1, emphasis zoom (native):** 16 updates in total. Max step 50 px; the zoom-in takes only about 4 updates.
- **B2, hook zoom with flash layer:** canvas mode for 27 rAFs, then native for 220.
  - At the switch: scale step −0.0022 (1.2 px) and a 44.6 ms gap.
  - No visual jump at the switch.
- **C, zoom-punch:** median step 26.5 px, max 43.9 px, one punch roughly every 433–466 ms.

What this means:
- The preview only moves geometry at project fps (Preview.tsx:393, `frameInterval` in syncPolicy.ts:233). The 50 ms gaps are likely caused by the headless rAF rate (a hypothesis).
- Native mode resizes the `<video>` through `style.width` and `style.height` (livePool.ts:435-441), not with a transform scale.

### Export measurement (`exportVideo`, full quality, H.264 from WebCodecs; box width measured per frame with ffmpeg, centre row, full-range luma)
- **exp_A.mp4 (30 fps, 120 frames):**
  - Max error versus the ideal easeInOut curve: 0.0004 scale (0.20 px).
  - Mid-ramp per-frame dScale 0.00309–0.00687, against an ideal of 0.00296–0.00667.
  - Max second difference 0.70 px.
  - So no snapping, no duplicated frames and no time error.
- **exp_A60.mp4 (60 fps):** error 0.26 px, max step 1.85 px.
- **exp_B1.mp4:** 1.000 → 1.032 → 1.110 → 1.154 → 1.174 → 1.180 (42.4 px/frame), and back down in about 5 frames.
- **exp_C.mp4:** 1.110 1.049 1.000 … 1.061 1.110 …
  - The clip starts already zoomed in at frame 0 (the effect runs on timeline time).
  - Each punch ramps in 2 frames.

**Conclusion:** export and preview reproduce the curves they are given faithfully. Motion looks unsmooth because the generated curves are punches or steps, there is no motion blur, and the preview updates at 30 Hz.

### Why "follow the reference" can't produce smooth motion
- StyleProfile (types.ts:552-565) only has `zoomPunchIns: boolean`.
- The analyzer prompt only asks about punch-ins.
- Frames are sampled at about 1 per second (frames.ts:122-205). The 0.25 s 48×27 diffs are used only for cuts and color, so there is no motion estimate.
- The demo sets `zoomPunchIns = fast`.
- `model.ts:125` adds alternating zoom whenever the pacing is fast.
- `edit-system.md:187` tells Claude to use "keyframes rápidos".

The result: a calm reference with slow push-ins comes out as either "no zoom" or "punch-ins", never as smooth push-ins.

### Recommended defaults for smooth motion
- **Easing:** `easeInOut` is acceptable (velocity is zero at both ends). Better: add `smooth` (smootherstep, continuous acceleration) and `auto` (monotone cubic through neighbouring keyframes) so multi-point moves don't stop at every keyframe.
- **Durations:** 0.6 s minimum for any zoom change. A push-in covers the whole shot (2 s or more).
- **Magnitude:** push-ins of 1.00→1.04–1.08; pans of 0.03 of the width per second or less.
- **Punches, shake and pulses:** only when the reference has them (measured `style.motion`) or the user asks.
- **Renderer:**
  - Preview geometry at display rate (native mode: CSS every rAF).
  - Compositor-only `transform: scale`.
  - Geometry effects run on clip-local time with smooth noise and envelopes.
  - Optional sub-frame motion blur in export for fast moves.

### Caveats
- Headless rAF was about 17.5 ms, not 16.67 ms, so the cadence irregularity in preview may not happen on a real 60 Hz phone.
- The Android jank cost of the native-mode width/height changes was not measured on a device. It is a hypothesis.
